terms.definition: Security method requiring two or more verification factors to authenticate identity
terms.example: Password (something you know) + one-time code from phone (something you have)

terms.definition: Software-based authenticator app that generates time-based codes on your smartphone
terms.example: Google Authenticator, Authy, Microsoft Authenticator

terms.definition: Physical device that generates one-time codes without needing a smartphone
terms.example: RSA SecurID token, AWS hardware MFA device

terms.definition: USB physical key that you plug into computer for authentication
terms.example: YubiKey inserted into USB port during AWS login

terms.definition: Protocol that generates 6-digit codes changing every 30 seconds based on current time
terms.example: The rotating code you see in Google Authenticator app

terms.definition: Primary account owner with unlimited access to all AWS resources and billing
terms.example: Email address used to create the AWS account - has godmode permissions

terms.definition: Service that tracks spending and sends alerts when costs cross defined thresholds
terms.example: Setting $20/month limit and getting email at $16 (80%)

terms.definition: Budget type that alerts when spending exceeds $0.01 - perfect for Free Tier users
terms.example: Alert sent immediately if any charges occur beyond free tier

terms.definition: Budget with fixed dollar limit per month (e.g., $50/month)
terms.example: $100 monthly budget with alerts at $80 and $100

terms.definition: Budget that tracks service usage metrics instead of costs
terms.example: Alert when EC2 running hours exceed 100 hours/month

terms.definition: What you have already spent so far in the current billing period
terms.example: It's day 15 and you've spent $30 - that's your actual cost

terms.definition: What AWS predicts you will spend by end of month based on current patterns
terms.example: Spent $30 in 15 days, AWS forecasts $60 by month-end

terms.definition: Percentage or dollar amount that triggers an alert notification
terms.example: 80% threshold on $50 budget = alert at $40

terms.definition: Email or SNS notification sent when spending crosses a threshold
terms.example: Email: Your spending has reached 80% of your $50 budget

terms.definition: First authentication factor - information memorized by the user
terms.example: Password, PIN, secret answer

terms.definition: Second authentication factor - physical device or app you possess
terms.example: Smartphone with authenticator app, hardware token, security key

terms.definition: Square barcode scanned by authenticator app to link your AWS account
terms.example: The black-and-white square displayed during MFA setup

terms.definition: Recovery codes provided during MFA setup in case you lose your device
terms.example: 8-digit codes saved in password manager for emergency access

terms.definition: AWS messaging service that can send budget alerts to multiple recipients
terms.example: Send budget alerts to email, SMS, or trigger Lambda functions

terms.definition: AWS usage limits that are free for 12 months for new accounts
terms.example: 750 hours of t2.micro EC2 per month at no charge

terms.definition: Individual user account with specific permissions - not the root account
terms.example: Developer account with read-only access to S3

terms.definition: Authentication method that cannot be tricked by fake login pages
terms.example: Security keys like YubiKey - physical presence required

terms.definition: Subset of MFA specifically using exactly two verification factors
terms.example: Password + SMS code (though SMS is less secure)

terms.definition: Physically isolated from other devices - not connected to internet or computer
terms.example: Hardware MFA token that never connects to network

terms.definition: Mobile application that generates time-based one-time codes for MFA
terms.example: Google Authenticator showing 6-digit code that changes every 30 seconds
